documents.t: Worked examples — executed notebooks rendered as pages (refreshed weekly against the live APIs): Quickstart

sportsdataverse.basketball.scb — 23 endpoints. Note: Unofficial use of a public source: these wrappers read the front-end API of the German Bundesliga sites (easycredit-bbl.de, toyota-dbbl.de), run by SCB; payloads are not redistributed as release assets. Note: Legal notice: the BBL Impressum forbids storing BBL content (Inhalte) in an information system without BBL's written permission. That is a copyright term, not a robots rule (the API host has no robots.txt). The owner reviewed it and accepted the intake (2026-10-12 ruling); keep requests slow (the runtime waits at least 1 s per host) and raise any published data release with the owner. The DBBL host is the same operator and API; its site notice was not separately reviewed. Note: Both hosts need two headers: a constant x-api-key and an x-api-secret that rotates. The runtime derives the secret on first use from the key embedded in an easycredit-bbl.de page (reversed, : turned into -) and never logs or returns it. The derivation was reverse-engineered from observed requests and responses and has not been checked against the site's own front-end code; if the site changes how it signs requests, every call fails with AssetFetchError. Note: Id key spaces: seasonId is the START year (2025 = 2025-26), so a wrapper's END-year season is sent as season - 1. Teams are keyed by teamId (seasonTeamId equals it in every sample). seasonPlayerId is per player per season and per club (a player traded mid-season has two); realPlayerId is the person. playerId is ambiguous (the seasonPlayerId in box scores, records and /season-players; the person in /transfers). Game ids are strings.
